entries.claim: The pinned Latin data give the Peter and Paul prayers in separate sections joined by the source's own rule Sub unica conclusione. The witness is a declared projection of the listed lines, not the program's rendered output, and a derived digital comparison, not an independent page image.
In a Mass of St Peter the prayer of St Paul is always added under a single conclusion; the rubric calls this commemoration inseparable and counts the two prayers as one oration.

The final secret has an audible Per omnia saecula saeculorum followed by the response Amen. Collects and postcommunions are priestly orations with a separate response. These rules determine the modeled boundaries, not the completeness of a date-specific commemoration inventory.

locator.section: Proper prayer of St Peter, rubric and commemoration of St Paul; RG 115a full conclusion

entries.claim: The component is an explicit same-edition composite: the Peter prayer printed without a conclusion and the St Paul prayer added sub unica conclusione on page 479, with the full conclusion of general rubric 115a in place of the printed abbreviation Per Dominum.

witnesses.independence_basis: Pinned upstream Latin data maintained outside this corpus, projected line by line from the cited sections under the source's own joining rule; used as a derived comparison witness only.

Both prayers are transcribed from the directly viewed proper page; the full conclusion is the literal formula of general rubric 115a on page xvii. No word is copied from the digital comparison source.

collation.recension: The 1962 oration with the inseparable commemoration of St Paul under a single conclusion, the full conclusion supplied from general rubric 115a
